You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 80714b09bc574c5b23e50264e76e6e0f78d23549 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Vladimir Kondratiev <QCA_vkondrat@QCA.qualcomm.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2015 19:10:48 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] wil6210: fix format specifier for dma_addr_t

Fix format specifier used for dma_addr_t, namely use %pad
Debug print virtual address for the same buffer as well.

Fixes: dc16427bbe65 ("wil6210: Add pmc debug mechanism memory management")
Signed-off-by: Vladimir Kondratiev <qca_vkondrat@qca.qualcomm.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@qca.qualcomm.com>
---
 drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c b/drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c
index 3cb4f35ebd05..8a8cdc61b25b 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/ath/wil6210/pmc.c
@@ -92,9 +92,9 @@ void wil_pmc_alloc(struct wil6210_priv *wil,
 			GFP_KERNEL);
 
 	wil_dbg_misc(wil,
-		     "%s: allocated pring %p. %zd x %d = total %zd bytes\n",
+		     "%s: allocated pring %p => %pad. %zd x %d = total %zd bytes\n",
 		     __func__,
-		     (void *)pmc->pring_pa,
+		     pmc->pring_va, &pmc->pring_pa,
 		     sizeof(struct vring_tx_desc),
 		     num_descriptors,
 		     sizeof(struct vring_tx_desc) * num_descriptors);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by using an incorrect format specifier for the `dma_addr_t` type when printing the address in the debug log. The original code used `%p`, which is suitable for pointer types, instead of `%pad`, which is specifically designed for `dma_addr_t`. This could lead to incorrect output or potential misinterpretation of the address value in the logs, making debugging more difficult. The patch corrects this by using the appropriate format specifier and also adds a debug print for the virtual address corresponding to the same buffer.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    <text1>

The original code used `%p`, which is suitable for pointer types, instead of `%pad`, which is specifically designed for `dma_addr_t`. This could lead to incorrect output or potential misinterpretation of the address value in the logs, making debugging more difficult. The patch corrects this by using the appropriate format specifier and also adds a debug print for the virtual address corresponding to the same buffer.
